thread:
maria: heads up — seeing a sudden capacity drop in us-west2. ~25% increase in Xid/ECC errors across many racks and autoscaler isn't filling. probe heartbeats drifting ~30s. anyone else seeing this?

infra-bot: ALERT: GPU_PROBE_HEARTBEAT_DRIFT - region=us-west2 - affected_nodes=48 - avg_heartbeat=32s - triggered_at=1725489123

ajay: i'm digging in. quick grep of node logs shows repeated nvml/Xid entries on rack-7 and rack-3. snippet:```
[2025-03-03T14:12:34Z] ERROR nvml: Xid 13 GPU0 node-rack-7
[2025-03-03T14:12:35Z] WARN probe: heartbeat timeout 31000ms
[2025-03-03T14:12:36Z] ERROR nvml: Xid 31 GPU1 node-rack-3
```

leo: are these soft ECC or fatal Xids? can we isolate specific GPUs? @maria can you paste `gpu-healthctl status node-rack-7` output?

maria: posted status:```
node-rack-7: ONLINE -> STALE -> ONLINE -> STALE (flapping)
gpu0: soft_ecc_count=124 delta=8 last_seen=2025-03-03T14:10:21Z
gpu1: xid31_count=17 last_seen=2025-03-03T14:12:36Z
probe-agent: heartbeat=31000ms backlog=8200
```

sarah: telemetry shows a sharp backlog in the probe ingestion pipeline right after the kernel/driver bundle that rolled last night (02:00 UTC). kernel/driver mismatch could cause nvml to misreport and probe timeouts.

jun: we did a targeted driver bump in us-west2 at 02:00 for the VM image. options: 1) mark failing nodes DRAINING 2) reprovision replacements from pool 3) shift routing to us-east1 until stable. agree on a quick mitigation? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ajay: +1. i'll start marking 20 nodes for drain (spread across rack-3 and rack-7). also enable fallback routing: `redwoodctl routing set fallback-region=us-east1`

maria: cost/impact note — draining 20 nodes will reduce available capacity ~12% in us-west2. SLA risk if burst isn't added. ops, can we spin up temporary burst capacity in us-east1?

ops-oncall: starting burst pool in us-east1: +80 GPUs (spot) — ETA ~6m. restarting `probe-agent` on affected hosts now. will update.

infra-bot: ACTION: drains initiated on 20 nodes by ajay - progress=0/20

leo: also seeing NVLINK errors on node-rack-3 in /var/log/syslog: `NVLINK: link error - flapping` — could be fabric-level. i've opened a colo ticket with networking (ticket# COL0-5532).

sarah: if it's a fabric issue hot-reboot may not fix physical link flapping. quick mitigations: 1) exclude affected racks from placement 2) prefer model routing to nodes with stable nvlink health 3) enable additional KV-cache routing so long-sequence requests are retried on stable nodes.

maria: applying temporary routing rule to exclude rack-7 and prefer us-east1 for heavy workloads. will monitor metrics.

ajay: update 15m — drains 10/20 complete. early telemetry: Xid/ECC rates on drained racks down ~40%. still seeing occasional heartbeat spikes on remaining nodes. continuing remedial drains + replacement provisioning. will follow up with a short runbook for postmortem.
